taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Acer saccharinum L.; Acer dasycarpum is an older synonym, not a second learner concept.
look_here_first: Find an opposite SIMPLE leaf with very deep, sharp, angular/V-shaped sinuses and a conspicuously pale to silvery lower face. Check multiple mature leaves, not a single atypical blade; confirm opposite twig nodes and paired samaras when present.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Approved Master Plant Pool row 13; 2026-10-07 taxonomy and diagnostic review; scientific-review-allium-acer-2026-10-07.md
project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas state-native under POWO/source-pool review, but a three-project-target-county native audit is not complete. Do not count in confirmed-native metrics.

morphology_keys.habit: Fast-growing deciduous tree, often associated with moist bottomlands; site alone does not prove ID.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, simple, palmately 3–5-lobed; lobes often long and sharply pointed, separated by conspicuously deep sinuses. Lower surface silvery or whitish; sparse hairs may also occur.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small early-season flowers may open before leaves; seasonal timing is supportive, not decisive.
morphology_keys.fruits: Paired winged samaras, often ripening in spring; inspect wing shape with scale.
best_field_traits: opposite SIMPLE leaf with very deep V-shaped sinuses
silvery/pale abaxial surface; some hairs possible
long pointed lobes, check several mature leaves
paired winged samaras, frequently early in season

comparisons.key_distinctions: Acer grandidentatum typically has broader lobes, less deeply incised sinuses, and may have short hairs below; leaf-surface pubescence overlaps. Acer negundo has compound leaves. Acer rubrum can show lobing but generally lacks silver maple's combination of extreme sinus depth and conspicuously silvery underside.
